Painful, firm right groin swelling 24 hours after cardiac catheterization; rule out pseudoaneurysm.

High-frequency linear (7.5–15 MHz) and curvilinear (3–5 MHz) gray-scale, color Doppler, and pulsed-wave spectral Doppler sonography performed over the site of clinical concern in transverse and longitudinal planes.

Gray-scale imaging of the right groin demonstrates a poorly marginated, heterogeneous, hypoechoic fluid collection within the subcutaneous soft tissues anterior to the common femoral vessels measuring 4.2 x 2.1 x 3.5 cm, consistent with a post-procedural hematoma.
Sac Dimensions / Luminal Patency / Lobulation: Not applicable (no pseudoaneurysm sac identified).
Neck / Tract: No communicating tract or neck arising from the underlying arteries.

Color and spectral Doppler interrogation demonstrates complete absence of internal blood flow within the collection and no communicating tract or "to-and-fro" jet arising from the underlying arteries.
The right common femoral, superficial femoral, and profunda femoris arteries are patent with normal triphasic waveforms.
The right common femoral vein is patent and completely compressible without DVT.
Surrounding Tissues: Post-procedural subcutaneous hematoma as described above.
Post-catheterization right groin subcutaneous hematoma (4.2 cm) with no sonographic evidence of pseudoaneurysm or arteriovenous fistula.
Patent right femoral arteries and negative right common femoral vein for DVT.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Painful, firm right groin swelling 24 hours after cardiac catheterization; rule out pseudoaneurysm.

subs.title: Findings
items: Gray-scale imaging of the right groin demonstrates a poorly marginated, heterogeneous, hypoechoic fluid collection within the subcutaneous soft tissues anterior to the common femoral vessels measuring 4.2 x 2.1 x 3.5 cm, consistent with a post-procedural hematoma.

Color and spectral Doppler interrogation demonstrates complete absence of internal blood flow within the collection and no communicating tract or "to-and-fro" jet arising from the underlying arteries.
The right common femoral, superficial femoral, and profunda femoris arteries are patent with normal triphasic waveforms.
The right common femoral vein is patent and completely compressible without DVT.

subs.title: Impression
items: Post-catheterization right groin subcutaneous hematoma (4.2 cm) with no sonographic evidence of pseudoaneurysm or arteriovenous fistula.
Patent right femoral arteries and negative right common femoral vein for DVT.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Pulsatile right groin mass and audible systolic bruit following femoral arterial puncture.

subs.title: Findings
items: Arising from the anterior wall of the distal right common femoral artery (CFA) is a well-defined, unilobular, pulsatile anechoic sac measuring 2.6 x 1.9 x 2.3 cm with no internal thrombus.
Color Doppler demonstrates classic swirling bidirectional flow ("yin-yang sign") throughout the sac.

A narrow, well-defined neck measuring 4.5 mm in length and 2.2 mm in width connects the sac to the anterior wall of the distal CFA, demonstrating a classic high-velocity "to-and-fro" spectral Doppler waveform (PSV = 240 cm/s).
The proximal and distal CFA, SFA, and profunda femoris arteries remain patent with normal triphasic waveforms.
No adjacent DVT or arteriovenous fistula is present.

subs.title: Impression
items: Patent, unilobular right common femoral artery pseudoaneurysm measuring 2.6 cm with a long, narrow neck (4.5 mm length x 2.2 mm width).
Favorable morphology for ultrasound-guided thrombin injection or compression therapy; vascular surgery / interventional radiology consultation recommended.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Persistent tender left groin mass 5 days post-angiography.

subs.title: Findings
items: Superficial to the left superficial femoral artery (SFA) bifurcation, there is a bilobed pseudoaneurysm measuring 3.8 x 2.4 x 2.9 cm overall.
Approximately 60% of the peripheral sac volume is occupied by concentric, layered echogenic thrombus, leaving a central/deep perfused anechoic lumen measuring 1.8 x 1.2 cm.
Color and spectral Doppler confirm persistent "yin-yang" flow within the residual patent lumen fed by a 3.0 mm wide neck arising from the proximal left SFA exhibiting a "to-and-fro" waveform.
Surrounding soft tissue hematoma measures 3.0 x 1.5 cm.
The adjacent femoral vein is compressed by the mass but remains patent without intraluminal thrombus.

subs.title: Impression
items: Partially thrombosed, bilobed left superficial femoral artery pseudoaneurysm (3.8 cm total size; 1.8 cm residual patent perfused lumen).
Extrinsic mass effect on the left femoral vein without deep vein thrombosis.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Follow-up ultrasound of known right radial artery pseudoaneurysm after prolonged compression bandage.

subs.title: Findings
items: Compared to the prior study from 48 hours ago, the previously documented 1.5 cm outpouching arising from the anterior wall of the distal right radial artery is now completely filled with homogeneous, non-compressible echogenic thrombus.
Color and power Doppler interrogation with low-velocity scale settings confirms complete absence of internal blood flow within both the sac and the neck.
The underlying right radial and ulnar arteries remain widely patent with normal antegrade waveforms.

subs.title: Impression
items: Complete interval thrombosis of the right radial artery pseudoaneurysm with no residual flow.
Preserved patency of the right radial and ulnar arteries.

bank.title: 5. Traumatic Pseudoaneurysm with Concomitant Arteriovenous Fistula (AVF)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Thrill and pulsatile swelling in the medial left thigh 2 weeks after penetrating stab wound.

subs.title: Findings
items: Pseudoaneurysm: Arising from the mid-left superficial femoral artery (SFA) is a 3.1 x 2.2 cm pulsatile pseudoaneurysm demonstrating swirling bidirectional color flow and a wide neck (5.2 mm diameter).

Arteriovenous Fistula: Immediately adjacent to the pseudoaneurysm neck, a direct high-velocity fistulous communication is identified between the mid-left SFA and the adjacent left femoral vein (PSV = 340 cm/s, low-resistance monophasic jet). The left femoral vein is dilated and demonstrates turbulent, pulsatile arterialized venous waveforms extending cephalad into the common femoral vein.

subs.title: Impression
items: Traumatic mid-left superficial femoral artery pseudoaneurysm (3.1 cm) with a wide neck (5.2 mm).
Concomitant traumatic arteriovenous fistula (AVF) between the left SFA and femoral vein with venous arterialization.
Urgent vascular surgery / endovascular consultation recommended (thrombin injection contraindicated due to concurrent AVF and wide neck).

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Enlarging, thin-walled pulsatile aneurysm at a cannulation site along a left brachiocephalic AV fistula.

subs.title: Findings
items: Along the mid-segment of the arterialized cephalic vein outflow tract of the left brachiocephalic AV fistula, there is a focal saccular outpouching arising through a 6.0 mm defect in the anterior vessel wall, measuring 2.8 x 2.1 x 2.5 cm.
The overlying skin and subcutaneous tissue are thinned to 1.8 mm.
Color and spectral Doppler demonstrate turbulent bidirectional flow within the sac without mural thrombus.
Overall fistula volume flow remains preserved at 1,150 mL/min without outflow stenosis.

subs.title: Impression
items: Cannulation-site pseudoaneurysm (2.8 cm) arising from the mid-segment of the left brachiocephalic AV fistula with marked thinning of the overlying skin (1.8 mm).
Urgent vascular access surgery evaluation recommended to prevent impending rupture; avoid cannulation at this site.
